How Can Video Game Movies Be More Viable?

Well new and new video games are more and more like movies. Should video game movies be viable? I think they should be an add-on think of the intro to a video game be a movie? or the end of the video game be a movie. Why redo a video game in a movie? Also older games are harder to make into a movie cause of lack of voice overs and too much content. Imagine FF6 in a movie it would have to me a 3 part if not longer, but I think that is the key is to break them up and not just make it one movie but that in more money then they will put into it.

They are entirely viable when they're done right. The problem with many older videogame movies is that the rights were farmed off to talentless directors like Uwe Boll as quick cash grabs. It's not that there's no movie inside the source material, it's that the people they're getting to make them see it as a consumer ATM rather than a worthwhile piece of art. VIdeogame movies of old were often rushed to try to coincide with the release of a game so it could milk the hype train.

For example, if you look at the more recent Street Fighter: Assassin's Fist entry in to the sorted line of Street Fighter movies, the people making the movie cared a great deal about the source material. They grew up playing the games and it meant something to them. As a result they made an excellent film. Videogame movies do not have to suck .

The person in this video is an idiot. He claims that you can't have a good videogame movie because movies are passive story telling while in games you're actively involved in shaping the story with your decisions. This is complete bullshit. It's entirely possible to tell a good story based on videogame source material without being in control of how the story unfolds. In fact, in most games (save those that have true branching stories) you often have little to no control over how a story unfolds anyway.

One word: License costs.

So long as a sizeable portion of a movie's production cost inevitably goes to the big publishers, you shouldn't be surprised that movies based on video games will almost inevitably be inherently inferior to movies based on their own setting that can use the cash in other fields.

A secondary thing to consider is that video game movies frequently are based on the assumption that the people who watch them are die-hard fans of the video game they are based on, and thus will watch even complete turds to long as it is related to their favorite game (see also: The Warhammer 40k movie that looks like a CGI short from the 90s).
